objective: Implement a Codex-owned, Tinto-projected subagent graph with thread-correct event routing, durable descendant transcripts, lifecycle and capability fidelity, and targeted controls without introducing a Tinto scheduler or generic provider framework.
forbidden_changes: Do not create a Tinto-owned subagent scheduler, generic provider framework, new service, database, dependency, manifest change, lockfile change, or speculative abstraction.
Do not map Codex close-agent behavior to destructive thread archive or delete operations; preserve parent/model-mediated close semantics.
Do not auto-resume restored child work, execute provider-derived values, weaken permission or approval boundaries, or merge child transcripts into the root transcript.
Do not edit frontend UI files, orchestration state, requirements, roadmap, Jira, release artifacts, branches, commits, pushes, PRs, reviewer requests, or any file outside the owned list.
closed_decisions: Codex app-server is the orchestrator and source of truth; Tinto projects, persists, and controls the graph.
Route every notification and response by provider thread identity before updating root session lifecycle or transcript state.
Represent child and descendant threads additively under the root AgentSession, keyed by stable Codex thread IDs with parent relationships and per-thread timelines.
Keep ThreadStatus, TurnStatus, collaboration-tool status, and agent runtime state distinct and forward-compatible with unknown fields.

Discover and restore descendants using Codex thread/list parentThreadId or ancestorThreadId pagination and explicit subagent source kinds; do not rely on default interactive filters or a fixed 100-row archive cap.

Persist enough normalized hierarchy, metadata, lifecycle, capability, transcript, activity, and result data for complete restart restoration; legacy flat sessions deserialize as roots with no descendants.
Target direct Codex turn/start, turn/steer, and turn/interrupt methods only when capability state permits; wait and close retain Codex collaboration semantics and close must remain parent-mediated.

Inherit and display Codex-provided role, nickname, model, reasoning effort, runtime, approval, permission, depth/path, and capacity metadata when present; bound and sanitize all provider-derived data.
Use the existing session, journal, app-server, bus-contract, and generated-contract seams.

acceptance_criteria.description: Root, child, and nested descendant events are routed to the correct thread-local timeline and lifecycle without clearing or polluting the root turn, including out-of-order, duplicate, and unknown-field fixtures.

The normalized public contract carries hierarchy, source identity, distinct statuses, capabilities, collaboration activity, results, inherited metadata, and bounded child transcripts while remaining backward compatible.

Journal persistence round-trips a root-child-grandchild graph and complete bounded child transcripts across restart, marks stale active work safely, and loads legacy flat sessions as roots without data loss.
Codex descendant discovery uses explicit source kinds and pagination, preserves all descendants beyond legacy list caps, and handles capacity or provider rejection truthfully.
Targeted inspect, follow-up/direct input, steer, interrupt, wait, and parent-mediated close command paths preserve Codex capability and approval semantics without destructive substitutes.
Focused app-server, journal, and bus-contract Rust suites plus the natural agent_console suite pass with no out-of-scope changes.
